arxiv-2006-09075.title: PERL: Pivot-based Domain Adaptation for Pre-trained Deep Contextualized Embedding Models
arxiv-2006-09075.creator: Eyal Ben-David, Carmel Rabinovitz, Roi Reichart
arxiv-2006-09075.description: Abstract Pivot-based neural representation models have lead to significant progress in domain adaptation for NLP. However, previous works that follow this approach utilize only labeled data from the source domain and unlabeled data from the source and target domains, but neglect to incorporate massive unlabeled corpora that are not necessarily drawn from these domains.

arxiv-2108-06590.title: Few-Sample Named Entity Recognition for Security Vulnerability Reports by Fine-Tuning Pre-Trained Language Models
arxiv-2108-06590.creator: Guanqun Yang, Shay Dineen, Zhipeng Lin, Xueqing Liu
arxiv-2108-06590.description: Abstract Public security vulnerability reports (e.g., CVE reports) play an important role in the maintenance of computer and network systems. Security companies and administrators rely on information from these reports to prioritize tasks on developing and deploying patches to their customers.

arxiv-2111-03014.title: Polarization and phase control of electron injection and acceleration in the plasma by a self-steepening laser pulse
arxiv-2111-03014.creator: Jihoon Kim, Tianhong Wang, Vladimir Khudik, Gennady Shvets
arxiv-2111-03014.description: Abstract We describe an interplay between two injection mechanism of background electrons into an evolving plasma bubble behind an intense laser pulse: one due to the overall bubble expansion, and another due to its periodic undulation. The two mechanisms occur simultaneously when an intense laser pulse propagating inside a plasma forms a shock-like steepened front.

arxiv-2204-07499.title: Endomorphisms and derivations of the measure algebra of commutative hypergroups
arxiv-2204-07499.creator: Żywilla Fechner, Eszter Gselmann, László Székelyhidi
arxiv-2204-07499.description: Abstract Endomorphisms of the measure algebra of commutative hypergroups are investigated. We focus on derivations and higher order derivations which are closely related to moment function sequences of higher rank. We describe the exact connection between those higher order derivations which are endomorphisms of the measure algebra if it is considered as a module over the ring of continuous functions.

arxiv-2307-13904.title: Schubert calculus in Lie groups
arxiv-2307-13904.creator: Haibao Duan
arxiv-2307-13904.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Haibao Duan. Let G G be a Lie group with a maximal torus T T . Combining Schubert calculus in the flag manifold G / T G/T with the Serre spectral sequence of the fibration G → G / T G\rightarrow G/T , we construct the integral cohomology ring H ∗ ​ ( G ) H^{\ast}(G) uniformly for any compact and simply-connected Lie group G G .

arxiv-2404-13658.title: Tripartite multiphoton Jaynes-Cummings model: Analytical solution and Wigner nonclassicalities
arxiv-2404-13658.creator: Pradip Laha, P. A. Ameen Yasir, Peter van Loock
arxiv-2404-13658.description: Abstract We investigate a generic tripartite quantum system featuring a single qubit interacting concurrently with two quantized harmonic oscillators via nonlinear multiphoton Jaynes-Cummings (MPJC) interactions. Assuming the qubit is initially prepared in a superposition state and the two oscillators are in arbitrary Fock states, we analytically trace the temporal evolution of this tripartite pure initial state.

arxiv-2410-03524.title: Steering Large Language Models between Code Execution and Textual Reasoning
arxiv-2410-03524.creator: Yongchao Chen, Harsh Jhamtani, Srinagesh Sharma, Chuchu Fan, Chi Wang
arxiv-2410-03524.description: Abstract While a lot of recent research focuses on enhancing the textual reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) by optimizing the multi-agent framework or reasoning chains, several benchmark tasks can be solved with 100% success through direct coding, which is more scalable and avoids the computational overhead associated with textual iterating and searching.

arxiv-2503-17605.title: Explainable identification of similarities between entities for discovery in large text
arxiv-2503-17605.creator: Akhil Joshi, Sai Teja Erukude, Lior Shamir
arxiv-2503-17605.description: Abstract With the availability of virtually infinite number text documents in digital format, automatic comparison of textual data is essential for extracting meaningful insights that are difficult to identify manually. Many existing tools, including AI and large language models, struggle to provide precise and explainable insights into textual similarities.

arxiv-2506-09496.title: EnerBridge-DPO: Energy-Guided Protein Inverse Folding with Markov Bridges and Direct Preference Optimization
arxiv-2506-09496.creator: Dingyi Rong, Haotian Lu, Wenzhuo Zheng, Fan Zhang, Shuangjia Zheng, Ning Liu
arxiv-2506-09496.description: Abstract Designing protein sequences with optimal energetic stability is a key challenge in protein inverse folding, as current deep learning methods are primarily trained by maximizing sequence recovery rates, often neglecting the energy of the generated sequences. This work aims to overcome this limitation by developing a model that directly generates low-energy, stable protein sequences.

pmc-10624311.description: BackgroundThe majority of childhood blindness causes in low-income countries are treatable or avoidable. Parents or guardians are responsible for making decisions regarding a child’s eye care. Understanding parents’ awareness and perception of eye problems in crucial in helping to know parents’ eye care-seeking behavior.ObjectiveTo determine parental knowledge, attitudes and practice regarding child eye health.

pmc-11405076.title: Prevalence and Associated Risk Factors of Insomnia Among Adults in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
pmc-11405076.creator: Hareth Almajid, Abdulrahman M Elnasieh, Alaa A Alnamlah
pmc-11405076.description: BackgroundInsomnia is a common sleep disorder with significant effects on physical and mental health. This study aimed to document the prevalence of insomnia and its associated risk factors among adults in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.Materials and methodsA cross-sectional study was conducted in Riyadh using the Sleep Condition Indicator Questionnaire (SCIQ). Data were collected from 548 participants.

pmc-12723827.title: Comparing diet-related attitudes, perceptions, and behaviors of vegan and omnivorous adults: results from a cross-sectional survey study in Germany
pmc-12723827.creator: Dan Borzekowski, Emilia Boehm, Natalie Berger, Ann-Kathrin Lindemann, Dino Trescher, Mark Lohmann, Gaby-Fleur Böl
pmc-12723827.description: BackgroundAs a well-balanced vegan diet is associated with reduced diet-related health risks, it is in the interest of local authorities to develop appropriate public health interventions to promote such a diet. In order to do so, it is important to understand the psychological characteristics relating to a vegan diet, so that they can be taken into account in the development.

pmc-12738746.title: Effects of bisphosphonates after denosumab discontinuation and treatment effect heterogeneity using causal machine learning
pmc-12738746.creator: Miryoung Kim, Nakyung Jeon, Hae Sun Suh
pmc-12738746.description: Discontinuation of denosumab is associated with a rebound increase in osteoporotic fracture (OF) risk, and bisphosphonates (BPs) are commonly recommended as sequential therapy to mitigate this risk. However, their real-world effectiveness—and whether certain patients benefit more than others—remains unclear. To address this question, we employed a causal machine learning approach capable of estimating heterogeneous treatment effects.

pmc-13090726.title: Recent advances in immunoregulatory biomaterials for tendon healing: From immune remodeling to functional regeneration
pmc-13090726.creator: Jinbo Zhang, Qing Han, Xue Zhao, Xingzhen Li, Aobo Zhang, Yang Liu, Jincheng Wang, Hao Chen
pmc-13090726.description: Tendon injury is a prevalent musculoskeletal disorder characterized by delayed healing, functional impairment, and diminished quality of life. Tendon repair is a dynamic process driven by immune regulation of tissue remodeling.This review summarizes the immunological mechanisms underlying tendon healing. In the early inflammatory phase, neutrophils and M1 macrophages trigger tissue degradation through TNF-α and IL-1β mediated NF-κB and MAPK pathways.

pmc-13146685.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A365 THROMBOLYSIS IN ACUTE ISCHEMIC STROKE CASUISTRY FROM RURAL LATIN AMERICAN SECONDARY ATTENTION MEDICAL CENTER

pmc-13612991.title: Current advances in metal nanoparticle-based stimuli-responsive nanotherapies
pmc-13612991.creator: Yao Wang, Qianpeng Li, Meina Yu, Yao Gao, Kirsten L. Van Landuyt, Wenyue Sun, Huanhuan Jiang
pmc-13612991.description: Stimuli-responsive nanotherapy (SRN) has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy that employs nanosensitizers activated by external physical or chemical stimuli to generate reactive species for disease treatment. Among various nanosensitizers, metal nanoparticles (MNPs) have attracted considerable attention owing to their unique physicochemical properties, including tunable optical responses, catalytic activity, magnetic behavior, and high surface reactivity.
